geometry_edits.rationale: Transform the dominant mass into a split-wing form so the street edge can be opened with a clearer public threshold while preserving a single readable overall body.
Introduce a modest gap to form a usable void rather than a purely decorative notch.
Keep the split aligned with the long axis so the mass remains coherent and the public opening reads along the primary body.
Strengthen the carved open-space figure to support the neighborhood public threshold.
Open the courtyard to the access side so the void responds directly to the frontage.

graph_edits.rationale: The current dominant mass reads too sealed at the ground edge; splitting the primary body is a structural way to create a clearer public threshold and improve entry legibility without losing the overall compact gesture.
Reduce the bend to keep one dominant primary mass while avoiding an over-deformed silhouette; this preserves coherence and supports a clearer hierarchy.
Simplify the sectional articulation so the mass reads as a calmer, more continuous neighborhood volume rather than a faceted object.
Increase the courtyard/void presence to make the public open-space figure more legible and better tied to the access edge.
Orient the carved void toward the verified access side so the ground response becomes semantically aligned with the street frontage.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent low-rise mass in all four views, with a consistent dominant body and a modest top condition rather than fragmented pieces. Parcel containment appears respected, and the silhouette is not a meaningless stair-step stack. The main weakness is that the verified access edge is not strongly translated into a public void or porous ground response; the building edge remains mostly sealed, so the street threshold is only weakly articulated. Program-wise, the mass can plausibly support neighborhood living/commercial mixed use because it is compact, low-rise, and maintains hierarchy, but it is still closer to a generic solid block than a clearly active street building. The reference reinforces the idea of a simple primary volume with a legible entry condition and small attached accent, which is partially present here.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is more pavilion-like and materially resolved; it should inform threshold and hierarchy, not be copied as a finished facade or standalone object.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise commercial massing with a clear primary volume, small attached vertical accent, and an entry-side setback/canopy logic that keeps the ground edge legible.

warnings: Access-edge response is weak relative to the required public threshold.
Open-space figure is underdeveloped; void logic is not yet clearly legible.
Program fit is plausible but not yet fully expressive of an active neighborhood ground relationship.
